purpose: Permit a previously trusted release-attestation authority to be reactivated only through explicit, byte-pinned rollback authorization.
rules: Rollback never rewrites or truncates authority lineage; it appends a new rollback activation.
The restore authority must have appeared earlier in the validated lineage and must reuse that earlier entry's exact workflow blob SHA.
The rollback receipt binds the currently active failed authority, the prior authority being restored, its original lineage sequence and its exact workflow blob.
All required rollback review controls are explicitly true and approval occurs no later than reactivation.
The reviewer id is explicit and may not use the reserved shine-defence-core machine authority.
The receipt is referenced by exact repository path and Git blob SHA; receipt-byte changes invalidate the rollback entry.
A rollback activation does not erase the failed generation. Future forward promotions continue from the rollback activation as the current predecessor.
limitations: Rollback authorization proves recorded approval and byte identity; it does not independently prove the real-world identity of the named reviewer.
Reactivation restores a previously trusted authority workflow; it does not roll back unrelated application or Foundation state.
